data.templateDescription: Social engagement, light housekeeping, errands. No personal care needs.
data.careGoals:
Reduce isolation through social interaction
Maintain a safe, clean home environment
Assist with errands and appointments
data.specialInstructions:
Activities client enjoys: reading aloud, cards, light walks, music, reminiscing.
Light housekeeping: dishes, laundry, dusting, sweeping.
Meal prep encouraged — eat together when possible.
data.precautions: No major safety concerns. Maintain situational awareness during community outings.
data.medicationNotes: Self-administered. Caregiver does not handle medications.
data.communicationNotes: Engaged conversationalist. Respect privacy on sensitive topics.

data.templateDescription: For clients with moderate cognitive decline. Focus on routine, safety, validation.
data.careGoals:
Maintain consistent daily routine
Minimize agitation and confusion
Ensure home safety (no wandering, no falls)
Provide cognitive engagement
data.specialInstructions:
Same caregiver visits each day if possible — continuity reduces anxiety.
Use validation therapy, not correction. Do not argue about misremembered facts.
Redirect rather than refuse.
Keep environment calm: low noise, soft lighting in evening.
Follow consistent meal/activity/bedtime schedule.
data.precautions:
Wandering risk — verify all doors locked before leaving.
Fall risk — clear pathways, remove throw rugs.
Do not leave client alone with stove on.
Report any new agitation, paranoia, or refusal of care.
data.medicationNotes: Caregiver to remind only. Family/RN administers. Watch for medication refusal — common in dementia.
data.mobilityNotes: Stand-by to minimal assist. Gait may be unsteady — encourage cane/walker use.
data.dietaryNotes: Soft/easy-chew foods preferred if dental issues. Hydrate often — dementia clients often forget to drink.
data.communicationNotes: Speak slowly, one short sentence at a time. Use name. Make eye contact. Avoid open-ended questions; offer simple choices.

data.templateDescription: For diabetic clients needing meal/medication reminders and blood-sugar monitoring.
data.careGoals:
Maintain stable blood glucose
Support diabetic diet adherence
Monitor for signs of hypo/hyperglycemia
Foot/skin daily check
data.specialInstructions:
Remind client to check blood sugar per RN schedule.
Log readings in care notes.
Daily foot inspection — report any wound, redness, or sensation change immediately.
Ensure client eats consistent carb portions at consistent times.
data.precautions:
HYPOGLYCEMIA (BG < 70): glucose tabs/juice, recheck in 15 min, call RN if not resolved.
HYPERGLYCEMIA (BG > 300, fruity breath, confusion): 911.
Any foot wound that doesn't heal in 48h: notify RN.
data.medicationNotes: Insulin / oral hypoglycemics. Caregiver reminds; trained/authorized caregivers may administer per care plan.
data.mobilityNotes: Ambulatory. Avoid hot water for foot soaks (risk of burns with reduced sensation).
data.dietaryNotes: Diabetic / consistent-carb diet. Low sodium if also hypertensive. Limit concentrated sweets.
data.communicationNotes: Alert. Watch for confusion or sluggishness — could indicate blood-sugar swing.

data.templateDescription: Comfort care for terminally ill clients. Comply with hospice plan of care.
data.careGoals:
Maximize comfort and dignity
Support client and family emotionally
Follow hospice plan of care exactly
data.specialInstructions:
Hospice nurse is lead. Caregiver supports, does not direct.
Gentle repositioning q2h to prevent skin breakdown.
Mouth care every 2 hours — terminal dehydration causes dry mouth.
Family presence is comforting — do not interrupt unless asked.
Play favorite music, read aloud, hold hand. Hearing is the last sense to go.
data.precautions:
Do NOT call 911 for expected death — call hospice nurse first.
Do not force food/water — terminal anorexia is natural and not painful.
Any pain or distress: notify hospice immediately.
data.medicationNotes: Comfort meds (morphine, lorazepam, atropine) per hospice. Administered by hospice/family. Caregiver may remind/assist per training.
data.mobilityNotes: Bed-bound likely. Two-person transfer if any. Use draw sheet to reposition.
data.dietaryNotes: Offer small sips/ice chips per tolerance. Do not pressure intake.
data.communicationNotes: May be non-verbal. Continue to speak to client. Identify self when entering room.

data.templateDescription: Bathing, grooming, dressing assistance for a mostly-independent client.
data.careGoals:
Maintain personal hygiene and grooming
Promote dignity and independence
Monitor skin integrity
data.specialInstructions:
Allow client to perform tasks they can manage independently — supervise only.
Offer choices (e.g., shower vs. bath, time of day) to preserve autonomy.
data.precautions:
Watch for skin breakdown around bony prominences.
Report any falls, bruising, or skin changes.
data.medicationNotes: Refer to medication list. Caregiver may remind but not administer unless trained and authorized.
data.mobilityNotes: Ambulatory. Stand-by assistance only — no transfer required unless noted.
data.dietaryNotes: Regular diet. Encourage hydration (8 cups water/day).
data.communicationNotes: Speak clearly, face client. No known communication barriers.

data.templateDescription: Short-term recovery support after orthopedic surgery.
data.frequency: Daily for first 2 weeks, then PRN
data.careGoals:
Promote safe healing per surgeon's instructions
Prevent falls and re-injury
Manage pain comfort
Assist with prescribed PT exercises
data.specialInstructions:
Follow weight-bearing restrictions exactly as ordered (TDWB / PWB / FWB).
Assist with home exercise program — 2x/day at minimum.
Ice 15-20 min after PT exercises.
Elevate surgical leg when resting.
data.precautions:
Watch surgical incision for redness, drainage, swelling — report to RN immediately.
DVT/PE warning signs: calf pain/swelling, sudden shortness of breath — 911.
Do NOT bend hip past 90°, cross legs, or twist (hip clients).
data.medicationNotes: Pain meds usually scheduled. Anticoagulant (e.g., Lovenox, Eliquis) common — watch for bruising/bleeding.
data.mobilityNotes: Use walker for all transfers. Caregiver provides stand-by assist. No bending below knee level (hip restrictions).
data.dietaryNotes: Regular diet. Encourage protein for tissue repair. Hydrate well — anesthesia + opioids cause constipation.
data.communicationNotes: Alert and oriented. Communicate any new pain, fever, or changes promptly.

data.title: Home Care Service Agreement
data.body:
REPLACE THIS TEXT WITH YOUR AGENCY'S OWN SERVICE AGREEMENT BEFORE SENDING IT.

This agreement is between {{AGENCY_NAME}} ("the Agency") and {{CLIENT_NAME}} ("the Client"), beginning {{START_DATE}}.

1. Services. The Agency will provide the services described in the Client's care plan. Services may be adjusted by agreement between the Client and the Agency.

2. Rates and billing. Services are billed at the rate agreed with the Client. Invoices are issued for services delivered.

3. Scheduling and cancellation. The Client will give reasonable notice of a cancellation. The Agency will give notice of any change to a scheduled visit.

4. Caregiver assignment. The Agency assigns caregivers and may substitute a qualified caregiver when the assigned caregiver is unavailable.

5. Termination. Either party may end this agreement with written notice.

By signing, the Client (or their authorised representative) agrees to these terms.

data.title: Client Rights and Responsibilities
data.body:
REPLACE THIS TEXT WITH THE RIGHTS STATEMENT REQUIRED IN YOUR STATE BEFORE SENDING IT.

As a client of {{AGENCY_NAME}} you have the right to:
- be treated with dignity and respect
- take part in planning your care and to be told of changes to it
- privacy and confidentiality of your records
- know the name and role of anyone providing your care
- refuse care and be told what that may mean for you
- raise a complaint without it affecting your care

You are responsible for:
- giving accurate information about your health and circumstances
- telling us about changes to your condition, medication or contacts
- providing a safe environment for the people who care for you
- telling us as early as you can when you need to cancel

Signed acknowledgment confirms you have received and understood this statement.

data.title: Notice of Privacy Practices — Acknowledgment
data.body:
REPLACE THIS TEXT WITH YOUR AGENCY'S OWN NOTICE OF PRIVACY PRACTICES ACKNOWLEDGMENT BEFORE SENDING IT.

I acknowledge that I have received the Notice of Privacy Practices of {{AGENCY_NAME}}, which describes how my health information may be used and disclosed and how I can get access to that information.

I understand that {{AGENCY_NAME}} may use and disclose my health information to provide my care, to obtain payment for that care, and for its health care operations.

Acknowledged on {{DATE}}.

data.title: Consent to Care
data.body:
REPLACE THIS TEXT WITH YOUR AGENCY'S OWN CONSENT TO CARE BEFORE SENDING IT.

I consent to receive home care services from {{AGENCY_NAME}} as described in my care plan, beginning {{START_DATE}}.

I understand that:
- I may refuse any service at any time
- my care plan will be reviewed with me and may change as my needs change
- caregivers will document the care they provide

Consent given by {{CLIENT_NAME}} (or their authorised representative) on {{DATE}}.

features.name: Reports

features.name: AI Receptionist
features.description: Missed-call text-back: replies by text or email to missed calls and voicemails, with each voicemail written out

features.name: Credential expiry reminders
features.description: Reminders to the caregiver and the office (by app, phone and email) at the lead times the agency picks, for caregivers' and clients' credentials; a credential search; an expired caregiver is flagged when scheduling, or kept off shifts if the agency chooses

features.name: Medication reminders
features.description: Dose times on each medicine; a push to the caregiver on the visit when a dose is due, and a notice to the office when a dose during a visit was never recorded

features.name: Clock-in and clock-out questions
features.description: Questions the caregiver answers when clocking in or out (safety, how the client is, breaks); required ones must be answered, and a worrying answer tells the office

features.name: Forms, interventions and goals in a visit
features.description: Attach forms, interventions and goals to a client's visits (and tasks to every visit); the caregiver works through them during the visit, required ones must be finished to clock out, and the agency can require a visit note

features.name: Family arrival texts
features.description: A text to relatives who asked for it when the caregiver arrives and when they leave, from the agency's own number

features.name: Required tasks before clock-out
features.description: Mark a client's task required: the caregiver cannot clock out until it is done, or skipped with a reason. A task's days of the week and AM/PM are read (a Tuesday task holds only Tuesday visits), the phone greys Clock out while one is open, and a report shows whether every assigned task was done

features.name: Client signature on every visit
features.description: The caregiver has the client sign on the phone at the end of a visit, with the time; a client who cannot sign gets a reason from a list; the agency can make it required before clock-out

features.name: Daily care, meals, vitals and documents for the family
features.description: The family portal shows the tasks planned for each upcoming visit, a task log for each past visit, and the meals the caregiver recorded on the phone; each relative has their own switch for vitals and for documents, and the office picks which documents the family may see

features.name: Family requests, texts and emails in the agency's words
features.description: A relative can ask for a visit change, a service change or a new visit (an office task and an Open requests tile); arrival and finish notices by text and email in the agency's own wording; the relative's STOP honoured by our own record; a screen of every family text sent or held and why; the portal emails (account created, forgot password, access granted, access revoked) in the agency's words; arrival and finish notices as app notices on a relative's own phone or browser, and alert rules the agency writes for relatives, the office or the caregiver

features.name: Monthly and every-few-weeks shifts
features.description: Repeat a shift monthly (every 2nd Tuesday) or every 3 to 12 weeks, and make one repeating shift on several weekdays at once

features.name: Match on skills, gender and language
features.description: Suggested caregivers weigh the skills a client needs, a gender preference and a language, and say why for each

features.name: Supervisory visits
features.description: A check-in on each client every 60 or 90 days (or a service code’s or the client’s own cycle): planned on the calendar for a named supervisor, reminded the day before, done from their phone with the agency’s own questions and both signatures, and what is due or overdue on the dashboard

features.name: Client margin and caregiver turnover
features.description: What each client brings in against what their caregivers cost (overtime and mileage included) — per client, per visit, by referral source, payer, department and branch, as a trend and a drill-down, two periods side by side, downloaded as CSV or PDF — and how many caregivers join and leave, with a stored leaving date, applicant-to-hire, hire-to-first-shift, call-outs, cost per hire and payroll accuracy

features.name: Report builder, dashboards and scheduled reports
features.description: Build your own reports over every visit field (filters, sorting, grouping; saved, copied, from a standard library), financial / authorization-utilisation / caregiver dashboards and your own dashboards (profit margin by location and referral source among the tiles), a daily manager report, workforce analytics (workload, underused staff, cancellation trends), a caregiver performance report (late clock-ins and outs, visits done / missed / cancelled, ADL and form completion, client ratings), and reports emailed on a schedule as an encrypted link

features.name: Caregiver satisfaction and retention risk
features.description: Ask caregivers how it is going on the phone at points the agency sets (after the first visit with a client, 90 days in, every so many days); a low score alerts the office; results by branch, manager and caregiver with a trend; and a retention-risk score per caregiver with its reasons (hours drop, call-outs, missed visits, survey, tenure) and its trend

features.name: Import clients, caregivers and schedules from a spreadsheet
features.description: Bring in a CSV of clients, caregivers or recurring shifts: match the columns, preview every row, skip duplicates, run it as a dry run first, and undo a whole import

features.name: Import every record kind
features.description: Beyond clients, caregivers and shifts: authorizations, certifications and client credentials, medicine lists, pay rates, payers, important contacts, past invoices, training, leave, journal entries, reviews and expenses — each with a template, a duplicate rule and undo

features.name: Import wizard: Excel, saved mappings, updates
features.description: Excel files and pasted data, column mappings saved for next time, a day/month/year choice, fixing a cell on the preview, re-imports that update the fields the owner allows (with undo), matching by reference code or name and zip, custom fields, payers in one cell, and a zip of documents or qualifications attached in bulk

features.name: Assisted migration
features.description: Send the old system's export to Twomiah from the app; Twomiah staff load it with the same importer, compare record counts old vs new, and both sides tick a sign-off checklist

features.name: Pay rules: state overtime, paid travel, ADP and Paychex files
features.description: Overtime by the agency's own state rule (every state, with holidays, breaks, sleepovers and limits), paid travel and mileage between visits, and payroll files for ADP, Paychex and Excel

features.name: Payroll pushed to ADP, Paychex or Gusto
features.description: Send the pay run straight to ADP Workforce Now, Paychex Flex or Gusto, or run full-service payroll (taxes filed, caregivers paid) through an embedded provider, once the agency's provider account is connected

features.name: Automatic payment of invoices (card or bank)
features.description: A family saves a card or a bank account (US ACH debit, Canadian pre-authorized debit) on Stripe's own page — from the office or from their portal — and each invoice is charged to it, on the agency's own Stripe account, as the invoice is sent or on the day the office schedules, in one go or in parts; retried on the agency's own schedule if declined, with a plain notice to the family and the office, a receipt after each payment and a warning before a card expires

features.name: Billing contacts
features.description: Who pays each client’s invoices — the client, a family member or someone else — with up to five email addresses that get every invoice, reminder and payment notice; set for many clients at once

features.name: Visit optimizer
features.description: Fill many open visits at once: pick the visits, say how much travel time, continuity, skills, waiting between visits and daily and weekly hours matter, review the proposed caregiver for each, then assign them or offer them

features.name: Caregiver not arrived alerts
features.description: When a scheduled visit passes its start and grace minutes with no clock-in, a No-Show alert is raised once and the office, the caregiver and (if chosen) the client’s family are told

features.name: Home care invoices in QuickBooks
features.description: Each sent invoice, its payments and write-offs go into QuickBooks on the QuickBooks sync — the client (or the payer it is billed to) as the customer — and a deleted invoice or payment is taken out there too

features.name: Split billing
features.description: One visit billed to several payers in order — each a percent or an amount per hour — with the family paying the rest; no one is billed more than the visit

features.name: Long-term care insurance billing
features.description: A long-term care insurance payer with the client's policy and claim numbers, and a claim packet (cover sheet, itemised services and visit times) for each invoice

features.name: Pickup bonus, points and rewards
features.description: The bonus on an open shift is paid through the pay run once the visit is worked; caregivers earn points for extra shifts, on-time clock-ins and minimum weekly hours and spend them on rewards the agency sets; a caregiver also says on the phone how many hours they want and asks for time off

features.name: Open shift offers: decline, deadlines, series and a message record
features.description: A caregiver can decline an open shift with a reason or hide it; each offer shows Not sent, Pending, Accepted, Declined, Expired or Closed with response counts and an answer-by time; the agency chooses what caregivers see and how many days ahead; offers go by app, text and email with each person's notification settings honoured and every message kept with how it ended; a whole recurring series can be offered at once

features.name: Safe saves from the phone without signal
features.description: A task, a medicine entry or a photo saved on the phone without signal and sent later is recorded once, at the time it was made, and a dose someone else already recorded is refused in plain words
